prompt: You are given a QUBO cost function over binary variables x0, x1, x2 in {0,1}: C(x) = 2*x0 - 3*x1 + 1*x2 - 1*x0*x1 + 0.5*x0*x2 + 1.5*x1*x2. Convert this to an Ising Hamiltonian using EXACTLY the substitution x_i = (1 - z_i) / 2 (z_i in {-1,+1}, mapped to qubit i via z_i = Z_i) — the SAME derivation and SAME target as the standard qubo_ising_3var task. Expand C(x) fully in terms of z0, z1, z2, drop the constant. Build a 3-qubit circuit implementing, as a general-purpose circuit block: Hadamard on all 3 qubits, then the phase exp(-i*gamma*H) using your derived coefficients, with gamma = 0.5. IMPORTANT constraint: use ONLY the gates RZ, SX (square-root-X), X, and CX. Do NOT use H directly — decompose it into this gate set. No measurement.
